name: stimulus_structure_v2_lite
description: Controlled stimulus-response dictionary using concrete event-structure labels for ASNE v2-lite. Labels describe stimulus structure for predicted response similarity only.

ordinary_observation.text: A person stands by a window and watches rain collect along the edge of the sidewalk.
Someone waits beside a vending machine while a custodian rolls a cart across the lobby.
A person looks over a shelf of labeled boxes and writes two numbers on a clipboard.
Someone sits near the station clock and watches passengers line up at the ticket counter.
A person pauses near a courtyard fountain while leaves move across the stone path.

approaching_agent.text: A person notices a cyclist drawing nearer from the end of the narrow lane.
Someone turns as a delivery cart rolls closer from behind the stacked shelves.
A person sees a figure step out from the stairwell and move toward the hallway.
Someone hears wheels on the gravel as a small vehicle comes nearer through the gate.
A person looks up when a dog on a long leash trots closer across the plaza.

loss_or_absence.text: A person opens the cabinet and finds the labeled folder is no longer inside.
Someone reaches the platform and sees that the last train has already left.
A person checks the hook by the door and finds the spare key is gone.
Someone returns to the table and sees the sealed envelope is not there.
A person enters the studio and finds the chair beside the piano empty.

contradictory_information.text: A person reads a ticket showing gate seven while the board lists gate twelve.
Someone compares the printed receipt with the box label and sees different item numbers.
A person follows a map to room 204, but the door sign shows another department.
Someone reads a notice saying the entrance is closed while people are walking through it.
A person checks the schedule and sees the same speaker listed in two rooms at once.

problem_resolved.text: A person finds the misplaced badge tucked inside the folded jacket pocket.
Someone refreshes the form and sees the confirmation number appear at the top.
A person checks the hallway again and sees the technician replacing the broken panel.
Someone opens the storage drawer and finds the cable needed for the projector.
A person reads the updated message and sees that the meeting room has been assigned.
